clue.text: Make-up artist follows old ladies around

indicators.note: to follow is to come after
around a date is circa, abbreviated ca, so here the word is itself a piece

explanation.surface: A make-up artist trailing after a group of elderly women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make-up artist' reads as one phrase, but the definition stops at 'Make-up'; the artist is a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain category: mascara is one of the cosmetics that make-up covers, the one for eyelashes.

clue.text: Rampant Royal Engineers team at last winning first title

indicators.note: a rampant heraldic beast rears up on its hind legs, so in a down clue the letters rise and read backwards
at last means at the very end, so only the final letter is taken

blocks.note: first = 1st, with the 1 read as I

explanation.surface: A victorious army engineers' team charging to the title.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading the digit 1 as the letter I is a common trick, and 'Rampant' only works as a reversal because this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: Mister is the courtesy title put before a man's name.

clue.text: Ancient Greek coin originally stolen by Duke of York?

indicators.note: originally means at the origin, the start, so only the first letter is taken

blocks.note: Duke of York is a variety of potato, and tater is slang for a potato; the ? marks the example

explanation.surface: A rare coin pinched by a royal duke.
explanation.walkthrough: Duke of York looks like a royal but is a potato variety, and the question mark flags that it is only an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Exact term: the stater was the standard gold or silver coin of the ancient Greek city states.

clue.text: Poor Matt Damon to finally sell shares

indicators.note: poor means badly made or in bad shape, so the letters are knocked out of order
finally means at the end, so each word gives its last letter

blocks.note: last letters of DamoN and tO

explanation.surface: A struggling Matt Damon is forced to sell off his stake.
explanation.walkthrough: The actor's name is split: Matt goes in whole, while Damon gives only his last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym in plural: an allotment is a portion shared out, and newly issued shares are allotted to buyers.

clue.text: King invested with a chap occasionally for capital

indicators.note: to invest someone is to clothe them in robes of office
occasionally means now and then, so only every other letter is taken

explanation.surface: A monarch honoured alongside a regular fellow, in exchange for money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' reads as money in the surface, but it is a capital city. The king here is two letters, not the usual R.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by category: Accra is the capital city of Ghana.

clue.text: Sabbath remix is a car crash

blocks.note: S is a dictionary abbreviation for Sabbath
a mash-up is a remix blending two songs

explanation.surface: A remix of a Black Sabbath track that is a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Remix' looks like it wants to rearrange 'Sabbath', but it is a synonym, and Sabbath shrinks to one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a smash-up is a violent collision, typically between vehicles.

clue.text: Fashion doll’s cape with a fancy border

indicators.note: to fashion is to shape or make, so the letters are reshaped into a new word

explanation.surface: A fashion doll's cape trimmed with a decorative edge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fashion' reads as the fashion doll, but it is a verb telling you to shape the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Descriptive: a scalloped edge is cut into a row of shell-shaped curves, a decorative trim.

clue.text: Clever canine escaping from lead

indicators.note: something escaping from a place gets out of it, so the letter leaves the word

blocks.note: a lead is an electrical cable
C stands for canine in dental notation; it is removed

explanation.surface: A smart dog slipping its lead.
explanation.walkthrough: The dog and its lead are a picture; the lead is really an electrical one, and the canine is a tooth.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: someone able is capable and skilled, which is close to clever.

clue.text: Case of taboo-breaking erotic photograph in the Big Issue

indicators.note: a case is the outside of something, so only the outer letters are taken
breaking into something means forcing a way inside

explanation.surface: A magazine story about a risqué, rule-breaking photo.
explanation.walkthrough: The Big Issue is a British magazine sold by homeless vendors; stripped of the magazine it is just a big issue.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a hot topic is whatever everyone is arguing about, the big issue of the moment.

clue.text: Heather goes outside and strips

indicators.note: to go outside something is to be around it, so the first word wraps the second

blocks.note: goes = urinates, in the euphemistic sense

explanation.surface: A woman named Heather stepping out and undressing.
explanation.walkthrough: Heather looks like a person, but it is the plant, and 'goes' is the bodily sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Noun sense of strips: peelings are the thin pieces pared off fruit or vegetables.

clue.text: Abrupt South American soprano returns to deliver slight

indicators.note: abrupt means cut off suddenly, so the word loses its last letter
to return is to come back the way you went, so the letters read backwards

blocks.note: LLAMA, a South American animal, loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A curt Latin American singer comes back to give a small performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'South American' reads as a person, but it is an animal of the Andes.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: small and slight both describe something of little size or importance.

clue.text: Old cricket commentator tucked into red dessert

indicators.note: something tucked into a pocket is put inside it

blocks.note: Che Guevara, a revolutionary, a red
John Arlott, the BBC radio cricket commentator

explanation.surface: A retired cricket broadcaster tucking into a pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tucked into' reads as eating, which fits a dessert, but it means placed inside. John Arlott was a famous BBC voice of cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by category: a charlotte is a pudding of fruit baked or set in a case of bread or sponge fingers.

clue.text: Incident with United supporter at the end of the day

definitions.text: at the end of the day

blocks.note: U = United, as in football team names

explanation.surface: Trouble involving a Manchester United fan after the match.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface sounds like a football incident report, and 'at the end of the day' is the football pundit's cliché.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: 'at the end of the day' means when all is said and done, in the end.

clue.text: Louis XIV maybe taking time to make bread

indicators.note: to take something is to take it in, so the king holds the extra letter

blocks.note: roi is French for king; Louis XIV is an example

explanation.surface: The Sun King taking a moment to bake.
explanation.walkthrough: Louis XIV was a French king, so he is named in French, and 'maybe' flags him as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by category: roti is an unleavened flatbread from South Asia.

clue.text: Drunk dad smokes without resistance in the bookies

indicators.note: a drunk staggers about, so the letters are thrown out of order
without in its old sense means outside

explanation.surface: A tipsy father smoking in the betting shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without resistance' reads as 'minus R', but 'without' means outside, so R goes in. Bookies is British for bookmakers.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: bookies set the betting odds on events, which is what odds-makers do.

clue.text: Sinner’s racket string ultimately broken by 19 – sweet!

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter is taken
something broken by an intruder is split open, so the potato goes in between

blocks.note: Eve, the first sinner; the 's attaches the racket
19 down is the answer to that clue, and a spud is one

explanation.surface: A tennis player's racket strings snapped, followed by a cheer.
explanation.walkthrough: The racket and string are tennis gear in the surface; the racket is noise. The dish is a British baked pudding of apples under sponge.
explanation.definitionFit: British usage: sweet is the pudding course, and this apple-and-sponge pudding is one example.

clue.text: Southpaw essentially boxed with 19, getting knocked over and knocked out

indicators.note: essentially means at its essence, its core, so only the central letters are taken
something knocked over ends up upside down, so in a down clue the letters are turned around

blocks.note: the answer to 19 down names a crop, and Désirée is a variety of it

explanation.surface: A left-handed boxer gets floored and knocked out cold.
explanation.walkthrough: The boxing picture hides everything: a southpaw is a left-handed boxer, but only its middle is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Medical sense: to etherise is to anaesthetise with ether, rendering someone unconscious.

clue.text: Harry Hill with rant under some powerful influence

indicators.note: to harry is to harass and disturb, so the letters are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: The comedian Harry Hill ranting while under the influence.
explanation.walkthrough: Harry Hill is a British comedian, so 'Harry' looks like a first name; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a thrall was a slave, so to be in thrall is to be held in someone's power.

clue.text: American relative drowning valley of cultivated land

indicators.note: something drowning is submerged, covered over

blocks.note: a ria is a drowned river valley

explanation.surface: A US relative flooding a valley of farmland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drowning' is apt: a ria is a river valley drowned by the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: agrarian means relating to farmland and its cultivation.

clue.text: Darkness is hell for plants

explanation.surface: A gloomy verdict that darkness is ruinous for plants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is' looks like a link but supplies a letter, as in the contraction 's.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by category: the nightshades are a plant family including deadly nightshade, tomato and potato.

clue.text: Kitty cheers up content from YouTuber

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means read from the bottom, so the letters reverse
the content of a container is what sits in the middle, so the central letter of You is taken

blocks.note: a kitty is a pot of pooled money
middle letter of yOu, the first half of YouTuber

explanation.surface: A cat video from a YouTuber cheers people up.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition hides inside a word: YouTuber splits into You, whose middle gives a letter, and Tuber, the definition. Kitty looks like a cat but is a pool of money.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by category: a potato is the edible tuber of its plant.

clue.text: Climb the top of Appalachian Trail

indicators.note: in a down clue the top of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: the smell a hound tracks is its trail

explanation.surface: An instruction to climb to the summit of the Appalachian Trail.
explanation.walkthrough: The Appalachian Trail is one name in the surface; split, Trail is the smell a dog follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym, noun: an ascent is a climb up a slope or mountain.

clue.text: What about promotion, boss?

indicators.note: about as in about-turn, turning to face the other way, so the letters reverse

explanation.surface: An employee asking the boss about a promotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Promotion' is the office sense in the surface, but it is advertising.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: the head of an organisation is the person in charge, the boss.

clue.text: Band of brothers released Samson easily

indicators.note: easily in the sense of loosely, without strain, so the letters move about freely

explanation.surface: A gang of brothers springs the biblical strongman from captivity.
explanation.walkthrough: Band of Brothers sounds like the war drama; members of this order call each other brother.
explanation.definitionFit: Descriptive: the Freemasons are a fraternal order whose members address each other as brothers.

clue.text: Relaxed dressmaker oddly flips

indicators.note: oddly read literally means by the odd numbers, so letters 1, 3, 5, 7 and 9 are taken
something flipped is turned over, so in a down clue the letters reverse

explanation.surface: A laid-back dressmaker who behaves strangely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' reads as strange behaviour, but it picks the odd-numbered letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to ease a grip or rule is to relax it, so both past tenses match.

clue.text: Piece from Norman Tebbit upset smoker

indicators.note: a piece taken from the words is a run of letters inside them
upset means tipped over, so in a down clue the letters read upward

explanation.surface: A newspaper article about Norman Tebbit that annoyed a smoker.
explanation.walkthrough: Norman Tebbit was a Conservative cabinet minister under Thatcher. 'Smoker' sounds like a person but is a volcano.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic-style definition: the Sicilian volcano constantly gives off smoke, so it is a smoker.

clue.text: Detectives match arsenic cases in definitive trials

indicators.note: to case something is to enclose it

blocks.note: As is the chemical symbol for arsenic
a Test is an international cricket match

explanation.surface: Police linking arsenic poisonings in decisive court trials.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cases' reads as police cases, but it is a verb. A Test match is a top-level international cricket game.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: an acid test, from testing gold with acid, is a conclusive proof of worth.

clue.text: Where unhappy couples may go right away to lift spirits

blocks.note: Relate is the British relationship counselling charity

explanation.surface: Advice that miserable couples might get away to cheer themselves up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right away' reads as immediately, but it splits into a letter and its removal. Relate is a British charity offering couples counselling.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym, verb: to elate is to make someone joyful and high-spirited.

clue.text: Rope in some to jam Grease

indicators.note: to jam something is to force it into a tight space

explanation.surface: Getting a few people to jam along with the musical Grease.
explanation.walkthrough: Grease is italicised as the musical, but it is plain fat.
explanation.definitionFit: Nautical term: a lanyard is a short length of rope or cord used on ships for securing things.

clue.text: Papers over attempt to get hold of Murray’s second serve

indicators.note: getting hold of something means grasping it
second as in second in line, so only the second letter is taken

explanation.surface: Newspapers covering Andy Murray's attempt at a second serve.
explanation.walkthrough: Tennis fills the surface, with Andy Murray and a second serve, but 'second' picks a letter and 'serve' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Phrasal verb: to dish out food is to put it on plates for people, to serve it.
